title: Python: TS, a local with one binding to type(self) or self.__class__ is treated as cls (DEC-303 (a22) item 3, (a23))
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3 admitted group TS: a local with exactly ONE binding, a plain unannotated assignment of type(self) or self.__class__ where self is the method's receiver parameter (rule 26) and type is the unshadowed builtin, is treated as cls: k.meth() looks meth up on the enclosing class's MRO as cls.meth() does, with the same polymorphic flag. Every binding of the local must be enumerable (item 2: enumerableBindings, no nonlocal or global rewrite, no del); a second binding, a rebound self, an annotation, a shadowed type, a write to self.__class__ in the class ((a25) item 3, later) refuses. No new rule: the (a22)/(a23) admission and the cls-receiver rule 26. Built per the other admitted groups: fixtures red before and green after with callee pinned and the full bin delta, positive twins, per-binding-kind refused fixtures, mutants by name observed red, and the five-pin corpus diff with every in-repo edge created or removed reported to opum-doc before the clear. Reference site: tqdm/std.py:91 cls = type(self), then cls.th_lock and cls.create_mp_lock().

acceptanceCriteria.text: k = type(self) and k = self.__class__ in a method make k.meth() resolve to the enclosing class method as cls.meth() does, each fixture red before and green after with the callee symbol pinned and the full bin delta

every binding kind that makes the local not single (rebind, del, for, with, walrus, nonlocal or global write, annotation, parameter) and a shadowed type or self refuse, with a refused fixture each asserting no edge and the bin unchanged, and positive twins

mutation checks by name, each observed red
